key_insight: A Swin3D Transformer surrogate can learn electrode-scale lithium-ion battery discharge dynamics directly from volumetric microstructure data, replacing expensive physics simulations with fast predictions.
engineering_relevance: This enables rapid, high-throughput screening and optimization of battery electrode designs while retaining spatiotemporal fidelity needed for engineering decision-making.
method: Swin3D Transformer processes 3D volumetric electrode microstructure inputs.
Gaussian Positional Encoding improves spatial representation of complex geometries.
Temporal Encoding captures non-linear discharge evolution over time.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation on an Electrochemical Simulation dataset and states the method outperforms state-of-the-art point cloud baselines while reducing computational overhead by orders of magnitude.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and representativeness of the simulation dataset, so transfer to unseen chemistries or microstructures should be verified.
paper_title: AI-Driven Surrogate Models for Predicting Electrode-Scale Discharge Behavior in Lithium-Ion Batteries
